issues: The 1647 father/patrimony claims are not independent human wealth, lifespan, medical or ancestry observations.
The first 4 categories of father significators are fourth house, fourth ruler, Sun by day/Saturn by night, and occupants in fourth; sect matters.
The author's father-own-nativity-preferable caveat limits what could be inferred from a child's chart and introduces additional historical birth-data quality conditions.
Good parent conditions involve source agreement between dignities, angles/succedents, benefic aspects and non-affliction; the variants are not independent empirical studies.
Mixed fortunate and unfortunate testimony is explicitly allowed, with discretionary strongest fourth occupant selecting among multiple candidates.
Jupiter/Venus and Sun/Saturn friendly contact for father longevity has several conjunction/aspect interpretation alternatives and is not an observed survival prediction.
The cluster of Sun, Saturn, Mars and Mercury glyphs in fourth on PDF604 has uncertain AND/OR operator scope; do not encode a categorical short-life rule.
Sun with lunar node plus Moon in fourth yields both father lineage and the native's life outcome; these are different target persons.
A masculine-sign/Mars-related glyph in the Sun/Moon paragraph is not securely adjudicated and must not enter a scoring algorithm.
The Sun/Saturn cadent/malefic clause contains a disputed glyph, potentially modifying a death prediction; preserve uncertainty.
The asserted death-by-melancholy is premodern medical language, never a diagnosis or a claim about an actual person's cause of death.
The chapter's father/mother relative descent comparison is historical social-class stereotyping; not evidence of ancestry, ethnicity or family standing.
No measured parent survival, income, residence, inheritance, age adjustments, pre-registered prediction window, cohort or class-matched control is provided.
The next printed CHAP CXXII mother section begins midway original PDF604; its substantive clauses must be extracted separately.
Only source images and selective anchored paraphrases are retained; no full diplomatic glyph-by-glyph transcription is certified.
